extracted.intended_audience: postdoctoral researchers applying for NIH F32 fellowships and institutional grants administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for preparing and submitting an NIH Kirschstein-NRSA Postdoctoral Individual National Research Service Award (F32) application, including eligibility, application components, and procedural steps for applicants and institutional officials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: To provide postdoctoral research training to individuals to broaden their scientific background and extend their potential for research in specified health-related areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The purpose of the Kirschstein-NRSA postdoctoral fellowship is to enhance the research training of promising postdoctoral candidates who have the potential to become productive, independent investigators in scientific health-related research fields relevant to the missions of the participating NIH Institutes and Centers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility: U.S. domestic institutions, Foreign Institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully read the Eligibility section of the funding opportunity for opportunity-specific organization eligibility requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: PD/PI U.S. citizenship requirement
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must be U.S. citizens or permanent residents; carefully read the Eligibility section of the funding opportunity for opportunity-specific PD/PI eligibility requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: PD/PI career stage and degree requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Career Stage: Postdoctorate/Residency. U.S. citizen or permanent resident, with research or clinical doctoral degree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The fellowship is intended for individuals at the postdoctoral/residency career stage who hold an appropriate doctoral-level research or clinical degree; verify any additional opportunity-specific PD/PI eligibility rules in the funding opportunity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding instrument and mechanism
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding Instrument: Grant. Funding Category: Research Training and Career Development. Budget Mechanism Code: TR - Training, Individual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an individual mentored training grant (TR - Training, Individual) under the Research Training and Career Development category; understand the implications for allowable costs and budget formatting per the funding opportunity and Application Guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentored fellowship requirement
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The F32 is a mentored postdoctoral fellowship; applications should include a mentoring plan and demonstrate commitment of a sponsor/mentoring team and an appropriate training environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference letters requirement
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must submit between three and five reference letters as part of the application; follow the funding opportunity and How to Apply – Application Guide for submission instructions and format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parent announcements usage and participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Parent Announcements are available. Parent announcements are broad funding opportunities that applicants can use to submit investigator-initiated applications for a range of popular programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parent announcements provide the standard forms and instructions needed to apply. Not all NIH institutes and centers participate on all parent announcements—check the participating organization in the funding opportunity before applying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow the How to Apply – Application Guide
rubrics_metrics.description: After identifying a funding opportunity, follow guidance in the How to Apply – Application Guide including any Fellowship (F) instruction call-outs, except where instructed to do otherwise in the funding opportunity or related notices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Application Guide contains required formats, page limits, and Fellowship-specific instructions; it supersedes other general guidance unless the funding opportunity explicitly states otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Due dates and key dates
rubrics_metrics.description: The Key Dates section of funding opportunities lists specific due dates. Many opportunities indicate Standard Due Dates apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must use the Key Dates in the specific funding opportunity. Note programmatic policy changes (example: changes for AIDS and AIDS-Related Applications beginning with certain review cycles) as specified in notices (e.g., NOT-OD-26-029).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application types and review cycle
rubrics_metrics.description: Review and Award Cycles: New; Renewal, Resubmission, Revision as Allowed; AIDS and AIDS Related Grant Applications. Scientific Merit Review; Advisory Council Review; Earliest Start Date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications may be submitted as new, renewal, resubmission, or revision if allowed by the FOA. Applications undergo Scientific Merit Review and Advisory Council Review per NIH policies; understand the timeline and potential start dates listed in the opportunity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participating funding organizations and fit to mission
rubrics_metrics.description: Each funding opportunity specifies the participating organizations. Applications must fit within the mission of at least one participating funding organization and meet all opportunity-specific requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the list of participating NIH Institutes and Centers for the specific opportunity (e.g., NICHD, NCCIH, NEI, NHLBI, etc.) and ensure the proposed research aligns with the mission and requirements of at least one participating organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre- and post-application NIH contacts and institutional resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Before you apply, check your chosen funding opportunity for application submission, scientific/research, peer review, and financial/grants management contacts. After you apply, find NIH staff assignments in the Status module of eRA Commons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Your organization's sponsored programs office or grants administrators can answer many internal and agency policy and process questions. For technical issues contact the OER Webmaster. Use NIH staff roles guidance to locate the right NIH contacts for specific questions.
